chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad from Abu Mas'ud from al-Hasan al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: What is the minimum number for the congregation? He said: 'A man and a woman.' And it is appropriate that the Imam be free from leprosy, madness, whiteness of the eye (a specific defect), and all other defects and profligacy, and that he not be one who has received a fixed punishment, which indicates this.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam (the leader of the prayer)
key_terms.مَحْدُودًا: One who has received a fixed punishment (hadd)

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum requirements for the number of people and the qualifications of the Imam in Shia congregational prayer?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defining the minimum congregation for prayer as just two individuals, highlighting the accessibility of communal worship. The narration further specifies that the Imam must be free from both physical impediments (like leprosy or madness) and moral or legal disqualifications (such as *fisq* or having received a *hadd* punishment), ensuring his suitability to lead the community in ritual purity and authority.
